column1: # KB-22 follow-ups + KB-23 — HD / partial-superblock encoder measurements, 2026-07-31
# base commit  999d295 (fix(encode): KB-22 was an unmodelled arm ...)
# host         Apple M4 Pro, Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, load avg 6.03/5.01/4.43 at start
# build        cargo test --profile test-fast -j 4, default dispatch (aarch64 NEON live)
#              (every row re-confirmed under AOM_FORCE_SCALAR=1 — see the .md)
# content      mirror-tiled first KEY frame of av1-1-b8-00-quantizer-00, bd8 4:2:0,
#              ALLINTRA usage=2, single KEY frame, 1 tile, stock knobs
# reference    real libaom aom_codec_av1_cx via aom-sys-ref; compared unit is the
# KB-19's is_4k_or_larger arm (speed_features.c:187-189) is NOT. perform_coeff_opt
# resolves 2 (not the 3 the 2160p cell covers, and not the 1 every sub-720p gate
# resolves). Speed 0, so KB-23 is not live either.
# Bite proof (stub -> fail -> restore), stubbing the arm body to
# and the asymmetry: 61 of the 62 aom-encode lib tests stay GREEN under that stub, the sole
# failure being the arm's own derivation test speed_features::tests::qindex_dependent
# --- Section 2: KB-23 — the speed>=1 partial-superblock divergence. ----------
# Sizes interleave exact multiples of the 64-px superblock with non-multiples,
# across the is_480p_or_larger and is_720p_or_larger predicates. All cq24
# 132x132 diverges at IDENTICAL total length (2407 == 2407) — a different tile,
# not a size effect. 480x480 diverges while 512/640/704 all match, which rules
# out any is_480p_or_larger framesize arm as the explanation.
# 250x250 was added post-fix: mi_dim(250)*4 == 256 vs a true 250-px crop, so the
# last whole 64x64's CNN window reads 6 rows past the crop. It matches, which
# retires the "non-multiple crops would need the true width" worry in
# extract_intra_cnn_window (the harness's extend_plane replicates from the true
# crop exactly as C's av1_copy_and_extend_frame does).
# The "pre" rows ARE the KB-23 bite proof: reverting cnn_root_whole_in_frame reproduces them
# exactly, while every SB-exact row is byte-identical in both states.
# Bite proofs for the derivation locks (stub -> fail -> restore, all restored, git diff clean):
# --- Section 3: KB-23 speed axis (same content, cq24, restoration off). ------
# The SB-exact speed-4 deltas are BYTE-IDENTICAL pre and post (-1 at 192x192,
# -25 at 256x256), and speed 4 stays divergent on all four sizes: the KB-23 fix
# does not reach into KB-21's cpu-4/5 band. That is what makes A->B attributable
# THIRD STATE, post-rebase onto 8a0faa7 (KB-21 root #3 — the quant matrix in the
# SATD trellis-skip arm) with the KB-23 latch: the whole matrix goes clean,
# INCLUDING speed 4 (0/8 partial-SB divergent, 0/... SB-exact divergent, speed-4
# rows now MATCH on all four sizes). That movement is KB-21 root #3's, not
# KB-23's — the pre/post rows above are what separate them. Re-measured in both
# dispatch modes at that base; the size axis stays 12/12 byte-exact and the
# --enable-restoration=1 at 1280x720 speed 1, base_qindex on both sides of the
# `<= 96` threshold that selects the LR unit size (speed_features.c:3095-3107).
# The restoration-OFF control at the identical cell isolates the LR path.
# THE PREDICTION DOES NOT HOLD. Even PRE-fix the port coded exactly C's
# restoration unit size on both sides of the threshold, and the coded size IS the
# derived bound — min_lr_unit_size/max_lr_unit_size reach the bitstream
# correctly. The pre-fix byte delta is IDENTICAL with restoration ON and OFF
# (-3/-3, +31/+31), i.e. entirely in the base encode: KB-23, not loop
# restoration. Post-fix all four pairs are byte-identical.
